# FDG9147

> AVOID overloading a method across `Span<T>` and `ReadOnlySpan<T>`, or `Memory<T>` and `ReadOnlyMemory<T>`.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.12 Operating on Buffers.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG9147
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: verified

Message: Give '{0}', which takes '{1}', a different name from its overload that takes '{2}'

FDG9147 reports an externally visible method that has an externally visible overload in the same type with the same number of parameters, the same ref kinds and the same parameter types, except that at one or more positions it takes Span&lt;T> where the overload takes ReadOnlySpan&lt;T>, or Memory&lt;T> where the overload takes ReadOnlyMemory&lt;T>, with the same T (type parameters of generic methods are compared by position). The report is on the read-write method, the one the body asks why it needs a writable buffer. The exception of the body is not reported: each method returns the type of its own differing parameter, as TrimEnd does when it returns a slice of its input. Overloads inherited from a base type, constructors, overrides, interface implementations and overloads that also differ in other parameters are not compared, so coverage is partial. Span&lt;T> and Memory&lt;T> types need .NET Core 2.1 or later, or the System.Memory package on .NET Framework and .NET Standard 2.0 (see FDG9137). Renaming changes the public API, so the fix is breaking; there is no code fix.

## From the book

If one method operates on a buffer in a read-only manner and another operates on it in a read-write manner, those methods should have different names to facilitate caller understanding on why the two methods behave differently.

```csharp
public static int Sum(ReadOnlySpan<int> values) { ... }

// Why does this one need a writable Span?
// It must do something different, so it needs a different name.
public static void Sum(Span<int> values) { … }
```

One exception to this guidance is when returning a slice of the input data, where the method returns the input data type, such as a `TrimEnd` method. As noted in earlier guidance, this overload set can be reduced to a single method if the method returns the slice indices instead of the sliced buffer.

```csharp
public static ReadOnlySpan<char> TrimEnd(ReadOnlySpan<char> span) {...}
public static Span<char> TrimEnd(Span<char> span) { ... }
```
